title: I Posted the Farmers-Market Scale Photo After They Rounded Up Twice

parts.text: I bought peaches at 9:40 a.m. The hanging scale said 1.92 pounds. The vendor, Art, charged me for 2.5 at the board price, then rounded the money again. I was thirty-one, holding a tote that smelled like fruit and dust. I asked to see the scale. He said city scales are suggestions. I photographed the needle, the board, the cash in my hand. Then he told the next customer I was a Karen who did not support farmers.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is naming me to the line while the needle still sits at 1.92.

social.video_title: The needle said 1.92 and the math said 2.5 — Part 1/2
social.description: Peaches, dust, double rounding, a suggestion scale. Then Karen. Would you have put the peaches back?

parts.text: The market manager has a certified scale. We reweighed. 1.91. Art refunded the difference with a look. I still bought the peaches. I posted the two photos on the market page without calling him a name. Support is a fair needle. Farmers deserve money that matches fruit. Karens, if they exist, might be people with cameras and receipts. I ate a peach in the parking lot. It was 1.91 pounds of fine.

social.video_title: The certified scale landed on 1.91 — Part 2/2
social.description: Refund, parking-lot peach, no names. Was a suggestion a license?
